question.leadin: William the Silent first led this country to its independance.
question.text: Name this country which fought the Eighty Years War for independence from Spain. Provinces in this country include North Holland and Zeeland (ZAY-lont).
question.clue: Its navy conducted the Raid on the Medway and was aided by the "Sea Beggars."

swap.leadin: This European country's colonial holdings included the Congo Free State, where enslaved workers had their hands cut off if they couldn't harvest enough of a certain crop.
swap.text: Name this country. Originally, its King Leopold II personally owned the Congo and authorized the Force Publique to commit atrocities to protect his investments.
swap.clue: One-third of the votes cast in an election in this country set up by the provisional government of Charles Rogier were left blank in protest.

question.text: The Dutch revolt against Spanish rule is generally known as this war, referring to its length. It was ended by the Peace of Munster and the independence of the Dutch Republic.
question.clue: Italian engineer Frederico Giambelli helped design fire ships during this war, during which Balthasar Gerard assassinated a leader.

swap.text: This operation attempted to capture bridges in the Netherlands using paratroopers and saw the British First Airborne Division meet heavier opposition than planned while trying to cross the Rhine River, crushing Allied hopes of ending the war by Christmas of 1944.
swap.clue: It was the last attempt to win the war by Christmas and had a strategic objective of forcing a crossing of the at .

question.leadin: This man established the International Association of the Congo and sent Henry Morton Stanley to explore the region.
question.text: Name this King of the Belgians who privately controlled the Congo Free State and amassed a fortune by extracting ivory and rubber through forced labor.
question.answerHtml: Leopold II [or Léopold Louis Philippe Marie Victor; or Leopold Lodewijk Filips Maria Victor; prompt on partial answer]
question.clue: E. D. Morel co-founded a group aimed at reforming a territory controlled by this ruler along with Roger Casement, whose namesake report detailed atrocities in that territory.

swap.leadin: This group was expelled from Taiwan by forces under Koxinga in 1662.
swap.text: Name this group that took Ceylon with Rajasinghe II under the Kandyan Treaty of 1638. It then lost both Ceylon and the Cape Colony during the Napoleonic Wars.
swap.answerHtml: Dutch East India Company [accept Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie; prompt on East India Company]
swap.clue: Members of this group waterboarded and executed English merchants in the Amboyna massacre.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the career of Belgian prime minister Gaston Eyskens (AY-skens).
question.text: Eyskens hailed from this Dutch-speaking region in Belgium's north, which he governed alongside the French-speaking Wallonia.
question.clue: One ruler of this region was imprisoned with his two sons for attempting to ally with Edward Longshanks due to this region's prominence in the wool trade.

swap.leadin: When you're a naval commander and you're all out of options, there's only one thing to do: set your ships on fire and ram them into the enemy!
swap.text: Fire ships were used by the Dutch to destroy English warships during this event, during which Willem van Ghent and Michael de Ruyter led a daring attack on an English dockyard. The HMS Royal Charles was destroyed during this event.
swap.clue: During this battle, which was recorded by Samuel Pepys, George Monck sunk many of his own ships to block the enemy's progress.

question.text: During the Dutch Revolt, this Belgian city was sacked by mutinous soldiers in the Spanish Fury. Despite the use of fire ships against Alessandro Farnese's pontoon bridges, this city later fell to Spanish besiegers.
question.clue: Echoing Rome, the people of this city affixed the letters SPQA to its pioneering Beurs building.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about an abdicated king.
swap.text: In 2004, Prince Johan Friso abdicated his claim of succession in this country due to past associates between his wife Mabel Wisse Smit and an accused drug lord.
swap.clue: This country withdrew from Formosa after being defeated by Koxinga, and it introduced technology known as rangaku through its control of Dejima.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about particularly old economic bubbles.
question.text: Tulip mania occurred in this nation in the 1630's when the speculation of Amsterdam-based traders drove the price of specific tulip bulbs incredibly high, only for the prices to suddenly crash.
question.answerHtml: Dutch Republic [or Republic of the Seven United Netherlands; prompt on “Holland”]
question.clue: A force from this country was defeated in a siege by a man who was born to a member of the Tagawa family and would go on to become the first ruler of the Kingdom of Tungning.

swap.text: In 1569, this type of map projection was created by the namesake Flemish cartographer. A standard map projection, it is noted for distorting the size and shape of large objects, thus making Greenland look huge.
swap.clue: This projection, created in 1569, uses straight longitude and latitude lines that make Greenland and Africa nearly the same size.

question.leadin: Yab Yum was closed when this city's court successfully argued its owner Hennie Vittali conducted illegal business there as a frontman for Hells Angels.
question.text: The Yab Yum brothel operated in the Singelgebied, which along with De Wallen and Ruysdaelkade comprises the Rosse Buurt of this Dutch city on the Amstel river.
question.clue: Princess Beatrix's 1966 marriage to a German noble was protested in this city due to his previous membership in Hitler Youth.

swap.text: This University of Leuven scholar, who created a 1569 world map, led the "golden age of Netherlandish cartography." This engraver, who coined the term "atlas," names a widely-used but controversial map "projection."
swap.clue: This Belgian-born cartographer is known today for his namesake style of projection, which distorts the poles.

question.text: The trade occurred as part of a 1667 treaty signed in this Dutch city that ended the Second Anglo-Dutch War. The Spanish capture of this city during the Eighty Years' War is memorialized in a painting commissioned by Philip IV.
question.clue: A declaration named for this city was issued in response to an offer from General George Monck and promised to pardon all who recognized Charles II as the British monarch.

swap.leadin: These people speak the closest related living language to English and Scots.
swap.text: Identify these inhabitants of a namesake island group off the coast of the Netherlands and Germany.
swap.clue: An incredibly strong pirate rebel leader of these people was named Pier Gerlofs Donia.

question.leadin: This city's first prince-bishop was the illustrious Notger, who had the Saint Lambert cathedral built.
question.text: Name this so-called "Athens of the North," if by "North" you mean "Belgium," whose greatest Renaissance ruler was Erard de la Marck.
question.clue: The strike of 1902, the second in a series of general strikes in Belgium, began when wildcat strikes broke out among miners in this province. This province faced a 1789 revolution called the Happy Revolution that restored the policies of Prince-Bishop Velbruck.

swap.text: In 1661, Portugal signed this treaty with the Dutch government of Johan de Witt. In it, Portugal ceded its possessions in Asia to the Dutch, but kept control of possessions in the New World and Africa.

question.leadin: Since their pay had been confiscated by Elizabeth I en route to them, angry Spanish tercios decided to carry out this action as a way of compensating themselves for their lost wages.
question.text: Name this 1576 action, sometimes called the Spanish Fury, in which forces under Sancho d'Avila pillaged a wealthy port city for three days straight. Rather than breaking the will of the revolting Dutch, this event instead strengthened their resolve.
question.clue: Otto Oberstein, drowned in the Scheldt while retreating from it, and the five thousand troops under the Marquis de Havre mostly failed to offer any resistance.

swap.leadin: Name these early explorers of Australia, FTPE.
swap.text: This Dutch Navigator and colonial governor became the first European to sight the coast of Australia in 1606.
